output: On October 1, 1999, BlackRock became a public company by selling shares at $14 each during its initial offering on New York Stock Exchange. By the end of that year, it was managing assets worth $165 billion and grew through both organic means and acquisitions.[23] A significant development occurred in August 2004 when BlackRock acquired SSRM Holdings Inc., a company specializing in risk management and analytics for institutional investors, from MetLife. This deal expanded its asset base to $325 billion and included State Street Research & Management's mutual-fund business within the acquisition.[26] In 2006, BlackRock merged with Merrill Lynch's division specializing in alternative investments (MLIM), which led to a new ownership structure where PNC had halved its stake and Morgan Stanley took over as majority shareholder. Moreover, throughout the financial crisis of 2008, BlackRock was granted access by the Federal Reserve for asset management.[35]

The third section discusses various developments in the business of BlackRock between January and October 2021. Initially, PNC Financial Services sold its stake in BlackRock during a $14.4 billion deal completed by January 2020.[49] This was followed by Federal Reserve's decision to involve BlackRock as the manager of two corporate bond-buying programs aimed at mitigating impacts from COVID-19, which included initiatives like PMCCF and SMCCF in March 2020. Additionally, these securities were backed by commercial mortgage guarantees.[35][50][51] Fast forward to August 2020, BlackRock was given the nod from China Securities Regulatory Commission allowing it establish a mutual fund business within mainland China. It became only then that this global asset manager would have legal standing in setting up operations there.[52][53] In October of the same year, they furthered their commitment to active investor engagement by introducing Voting Choice program for its institutional clients invested with index funds—this allowed them a say during shareholder voting on company-specific issues or general policies outlined in 14 different approaches.[54][55]

In February 2010, Barclays sold its BGI unit including iShares for $13.5 billion to help recover from the financial crisis of 2008 and as part of capital raising efforts. This move subsequently allowed BlackRock's acquisition of a nearly 20% stake in their company, leading them to enter into S&P 500 components by April 1, 2011. The financial success was evident when Fortune listed BlackRock among the most admired companies worldwide in 2013 and recognized it as having $4 trillion under management making it the world's biggest asset manager at the end of that year with around 65% institutional investors’ assets. By June 30, 2015, BlackRock had managed to grow its portfolio further by acquiring FutureAdvisor for $600 million on August 26, 2015; this new acquisition would function as a part of BRS with the intention that it operates within. Despite some setbacks in hedge fund investments leading BlackRock to wind down its only global macro dedicated fund called Global Ascent by November 2015, their overall growth and asset management remained strong.

In Part 4 of BlackRock's investment activities, they have been engaging with company boards and managers while representing their non-voting clients. In November 2021, BlackRock shifted its focus by lowering Indian market exposure but increasing Chinese investments through an India Fund invested in startups like Byju's, Paytm, Pine Labs among others.[59][60] Coordinating with President Zelensky of Ukraine on December 28, BlackRock committed to playing a role in post-conflict reconstruction. Following their pro bono advisory work for the same purpose ending in 2024 and no longer having an active mandate due to increased uncertainty,[63] they undertook asset management by selling Signature Bank's $114 billion assets of Silicon Valley Bank after a banking crisis.[64][65] Later, BlackRock filed applications for launching Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs with the SEC which were approved in January 2024. The first spot bitcoin fund reached $1 billion on January 19, 2024.[67]

In this text section: In January 2024, Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) was launched and reported as having almost $20 billion by May of that year. By April 2025, BlackRock had proposed to launch a blockchain-registered share class for its large money market fund. Then in June 2025, they introduced the iShares Texas Equity ETF (TEXN), an investment focused on companies based in Texas.

In July 2023, Amin H. Nasser was appointed to Saudi Aramco board as a replacement for Bader Alsaad vacancy in 2024 at BlackRock.[69] In the same month, Jio Financial Services entered asset management business with BlackRock through joint venture named "Jio BlackRock".[70] Following this partnership, New Zealand signed a contract to establish NZ$2 billion fund for renewable energy projects in August 2023.[71][72] In January 2024, the firm announced its plan to acquire Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) investment fund worth $12.5billion with a payment of $3 billion cash and shares for complete deal in March 2024.[73][74] BlackRock launched BUIDL tokenized U.S Treasury bill based Ethereum Fund, which managed assets exceeding $245 million within its initial week during the same month of acquisition plans with GIP fund launches and expands their headquarters in mid-2024.[76] Furthermore, BlackRock launched European Bitcoin Exchange Traded Product (ETP) called iShares Bitcoin ETP domiciled in Switzerland under Swiss regulations during March 2025 at Paris office as it seeks to extend its digital assets operation into Europe.
